title: Decoupled Pick-Only Imitation Learning Architecture, Spatial Obstacle Clearing & Continuous Workspace Radar
paragraphs: In today's session, we completed a major consolidation of our perception architecture by formally retiring the redundant Camera Feeds panel and elevating our computer vision subsystem into a unified Perception panel (panel-perception). With the wrist/side camera (Camera 2) permanently canceled, all operations are streamlined around our overhead Logitech C270 sensor (Camera 1) running 30 FPS OpenCV ArUco tracking. We engineered an interactive 2D SVG Workspace Radar mapping the continuous 30cm x 25cm manipulation pad in an exact 6:5 (1.20:1) physical aspect ratio, featuring real-time coordinate axes (+X red, +Y green), moving target puck with orientation vector theta, and digital coordinate telemetry cards. In the 3D WebGL Digital Twin, we refined the flight navigation HUD to start collapsed by default upon server boot and hard refresh, keeping the CAD viewport clean.

During an in-depth review of our first 30 human teleoperation demonstrations, we identified that while visual block acquisition was accurately captured, swinging the arm to the left to drop blocks introduced significant multimodal variance in release positions and heights. In Behavioral Cloning and Action Chunking, this variance leads to trajectory averaging and inconsistent drop heights. To resolve this, we formulated a decoupled task decomposition: the neural policy (BC or ACT) exclusively learns the vision-guided pick sequence (Home -> Approach -> Align theta -> Descend -> Grasp -> Lift to clearance), while the place phase is delegated to a deterministic, zero-jerk Cosine S-Curve trajectory moving to calibrated, persistent drop coordinates (drop_locations.json). For Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT), this reduces trajectory length from ~300 steps down to ~60-90 monotonic steps, eliminating trajectory reversals and accelerating model convergence.

For multi-block sorting with Block 1 (Tag 0) and Block 2 (Tag 1) simultaneously in the workspace, we devised a proximity-based spatial sweep rule. Because drop containers are positioned outside the workspace to the left (in the +X lateral direction), the autonomous scheduler prioritizes picking the block with the higher X coordinate first. By clearing the downstream object nearest the drop zone first, the subsequent block transfer traverses an entirely vacant table, mathematically eliminating block-on-block collisions without requiring exaggerated clearance heights. Finally, we codified a strict architectural mandate: the Servo Control panel (Servo 5 card) is the sole authoritative source of truth for the dynamic Gripper Open Angle (persisted in localStorage and kinematics_config.json). Hardcoded 140° gripper angles are strictly eliminated; all homing routines, autonomous standbys, and drop pose releases dynamically execute the active user-calibrated openAngle.

title: Continuous Autonomous Mode Redesign (Before vs After) & Three.js 3D Mesh Table Penetration Prevention
paragraphs: In today's session, we completely overhauled the Autonomous Mode execution flow to prepare for our upcoming journal paper evaluation trials. In our previous Phase D implementation, each registered policy model (v1, v2, v3) had an individual manual launch button on the UI card, requiring the operator to manually click 'Start Autonomous Pick & Place' each time a block was placed. Furthermore, the previous system lacked perception stability verification, meaning placing a block by hand could prematurely trigger execution mid-placement, and having the drop box within camera view risked false duplicate picks.

We resolved these bottlenecks by building a unified Continuous Autonomous Execution Engine featuring a Master Control Bar with a dynamic model selector dropdown and single Start/Stop toggle button. The arm now parks in a safe Standby pose at Home ([90°, 90°, 90°, 90°, 90°, openAngle]) while continuously monitoring the 25cm x 30cm manipulation pad via Camera 1. When a target block (ArUco ID 0) is placed, the system automatically initiates a 1.0-second stationary stability countdown (Δx ≤ 0.8 cm, Δy ≤ 0.8 cm, Δθ ≤ 15°). Any human hand movement or block displacement instantly resets the countdown. Once 1.0s stability is verified, the selected policy rolls out the 30Hz trajectory, deposits the block into the target box, smoothly returns to Home, and immediately re-enters Standby ready for the next block. The overhead camera field-of-view is strictly decoupled from the drop location, permanently eliminating duplicate pick triggers.

To solve the physical issue of the robotic arm and gripper occasionally slamming into the workspace table during manual teleoperation and autonomous rollouts, we implemented a 100% Digital Twin-based Table Penetration Prevention and Safe Revert Geofencing system. In strict compliance with our project's core research philosophy, this solution operates with ZERO complex analytical kinematics equations. Instead, it tests candidate joint angles on the Three.js 3D scene-graph groups off-screen, computes the exact world elevation (Y_min in mm) of the gripper claws via THREE.Box3().setFromObject(this.wristPitchGroup), and compares it against an 8.0 mm safety floor threshold above the tabletop (table wood at Y = 0 mm, calibrated pad at Y = 1.6 mm, leaving a 6.4 mm air cushion).

This safety guard is universally enforced across manual sliders, PS5 DualSense teleoperation (intercepted pre-flight in throttledSendAngles()), and live autonomous mode execution. If candidate angles command claws below 8.0 mm, transmission is blocked, a flashing crimson HUD banner ('TABLE PENETRATION DETECTED: REVERTED TO SAFE POSE') alerts the operator, colliding claws highlight in red, and the arm is held at the last safe pose. We updated all safe fallbacks to dynamically resolve the user's calibrated gripper openAngle rather than hardcoding 140°, and added a header toggle button ('Table Safety: OFF' by default, toggleable to 'ON') with browser localStorage persistence to provide full operator control.

title: 3D WebGL Digital Twin Simulation Engine (Three.js) & Dedicated ROS 2 Architecture
paragraphs: In this session, we engineered and deployed a dedicated 3D WebGL Digital Twin simulation engine on the web dashboard (panel-digital-twin), completely offline without external CDN dependencies. Built on Three.js, OrbitControls, and STLLoader, the digital twin loads the genuine CAD STL mesh components of our 6-DOF robotic arm (Base.STL, Waist.STL, Arm 01.STL, Arm 02 v3.STL, Arm 03.STL, Gripper base.STL, and Gripper 1.STL). The simulator constructs a hierarchical kinematic scene-graph (waistGroup -> shoulderGroup -> elbowGroup -> wristRollGroup -> wristPitchGroup -> clawLeftGroup / clawRightGroup) with exact physical joint pivot offsets (Base turntable height 56mm, shoulder pivot L1 95mm, arm link L2 120mm, elbow link L3 100mm, and gripper mount 60mm) and studio lighting.

The digital twin is connected directly to the dashboard's live WebSocket (/ws) telemetry stream, interpolating physical servo angles [θ1..θ6] at 60 FPS using smooth lerp integration. We implemented interactive OrbitControls (drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, right-click to pan), a persistent claw tuner interface for fine mesh calibration, camera reset presets, and an overlay displaying real-time joint angles and ArUco target block tracking in the 3D space.

Additionally, we decoupled the ROS 2 integration into its own dedicated dashboard panel (panel-ros). The new panel displays the full ROS 2 computational graph visualization (robot_state_publisher, joint_state_broadcaster, rosbridge_websocket, arm_controller), active topic monitors (/joint_states, /robot_description, /tf, /arm_controller/joint_trajectory), the TF2 transform tree hierarchy, and URDF/Xacro pipeline specifications, bridging our lightweight web dashboard with standard ROS 2 robotics middleware.

title: Behavior Cloning Policy v1 Deployment, Zero-IK Tri-Anchor Joint-Space Blending & Autonomous Execution Subsystem
paragraphs: In today's session, we achieved a major project milestone by completing Phase D: training and deploying our first end-to-end Behavior Cloning (BC) imitation learning policy (v1) across all 30 recorded human demonstration episodes (17,824 state-action frames sampled at 30Hz). The policy network ingests a 9-dimensional observation vector [θ1, θ2, θ3, θ4, θ5, gripper, X_block, Y_block, theta_block] and predicts smooth 6-dimensional motor actions [θ1', θ2', θ3', θ4', θ5', gripper']. Training completed in 5.9 seconds with loss converging to 0.5026 and joint angle Mean Squared Error reaching sub-degree precision (0.4038 degrees). We established a persistent model registry and integrated the Autonomous Mode panel on the web dashboard (http://localhost:8050/#panel-autonomous) featuring live Camera 1 ArUco perception lock, dynamic 6-phase state tracking, 30Hz joint telemetry stream, and 1-click execution.

During initial autonomous physical trials, we observed a 20% to 30% baseline success rate and diagnosed the core root causes: an inverted coordinate aspect ratio during feature normalization and non-linear spatial inaccuracy from single-demonstration linear offset heuristics. In accordance with our strict non-Inverse Kinematics architectural mandate, we corrected the physical workspace dimensions to X = 30.0 cm (horizontal width) and Y = 25.0 cm (forward reach/depth) and retrained the policy network. To eliminate spatial error without using Inverse Kinematics, we implemented Tri-Anchor Joint-Space Trajectory Blending using normalized Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) across the 3 nearest human demonstrations on the joint manifold (θ1..θ5), synthesizing continuous, collision-safe joint trajectories for any coordinate in the grid while widening the gripper approach angle to 148 degrees for physical capture tolerance.

Finally, we completed model lifecycle management and UI polish on the Autonomous Mode dashboard panel. We introduced a full deletion pipeline with backend endpoints (DELETE /api/models/{model_id}) and frontend confirmation controls, allowing users to permanently delete and unregister experimental model versions (such as v2). Additionally, we purged all emoji characters across the entire dashboard interface, scripts, and codebase to ensure a clean, professional, and publication-ready system.

title: 25cm × 30cm Workspace Grid Definition & Progressive 30/60/90 Demonstration Strategy
paragraphs: In today's session, we verified live computer vision tracking of ArUco Tag ID 2 (World Origin) alongside ArUco Tag ID 0 (Block 1) on the live Camera 1 stream. The system successfully renders real-time coordinate axes (+X red, +Y green), a connecting vector line with distance in centimeters, and exact block rotation theta.

We established a 25cm x 30cm workspace grid (total area 750 cm²) positioned directly in front of the robotic arm on the 50cm x 50cm wooden platform. The workspace is divided into 30 sub-squares of 5cm x 5cm each (5 columns x 6 rows). We adopted an iterative evaluation protocol: collecting 30 demonstrations (1 per cell) for initial baseline training, expanding to 60 demonstrations to evaluate orientation invariance, and reaching 90 demonstrations (3 per cell) to achieve high convergence and accuracy before moving on to multi-block color/tag sorting.

title: 25cm × 25cm Workspace Definition & 75-Episode Demonstration Collection Strategy
paragraphs: In today's session, we formally defined the Stage 1 workspace dimensions and demonstration collection protocol for our capstone imitation learning dataset. We established a strict 25cm x 25cm physical workspace grid (total area 625 cm²) on the platform board. To ensure dense spatial coverage and complete rotation invariance across the entire placement region, we adopted a 5x5 grid strategy (25 sub-squares of 5cm x 5cm each) with a target dataset volume of 75 demonstration episodes (3 clean human teleoperation demonstrations per cell across varying block approach angles and rotations).

Furthermore, we updated the Phase C Demonstration Dataset Recording Engine to record 5 primary joint angles [θ1, θ2, θ3, θ4, θ5] alongside binary gripper state (0 = OPEN, 1 = CLOSED), completely decoupling dataset trajectory logs from physical servo gear slip. We enhanced the dashboard Gripper state paradigm with dual-layer browser localStorage and backend kinematics configuration persistence, ensuring custom open and closed calibration angles stay preserved across reloads. The PS5 controller teleoperation loop was also upgraded with continuous velocity integration, eliminating Base motor lag and state conflict resets.

title: Physical Servo Hardware Assembly, Power Rail Debugging & Spaced Channel Protocol
paragraphs: In today's session, we commenced physical 6-DOF robotic arm hardware wiring and mechanical assembly on our 50cm x 50cm wooden platform board. We wired the Arduino Uno (VCC to 5V, GND to GND, A4 to SDA, A5 to SCL) to the PCA9685 16-channel PWM driver and connected external 5V/6V power. During initial testing of the Base Servo (Channel 0), we diagnosed a hardware power delivery issue where the PCA9685 onboard reverse-polarity protection MOSFET had high contact resistance. Bypassing the screw terminal by feeding battery positive (+) directly into the PCA9685 V+ pin header restored 100% full power to the servo rail.

To eliminate physical servo cable crowding on the PCA9685 board, we updated our control architecture and production Arduino firmware (robot_driver.ino) to use spaced even channels [Channels 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10]. We successfully mounted and tested the physical Base (Ch 0), Shoulder (Ch 2), and Elbow (Ch 4) joints, confirming smooth zero-jerk movement and precise slider responsiveness across all three assembled arm segments.

title: Phase C Demonstration Dataset Recording Engine, 30Hz Trajectory Sampler & Smooth Replay Architecture
paragraphs: In today's session, we designed and deployed the Phase C Demonstration Dataset Recording and Trajectory Replay System on the Web Control Dashboard (http://localhost:8050) Dataset Management panel. The engine implements a real-time 30Hz trajectory sampler that records human teleoperation demonstration episodes into persistent time-series JSON arrays containing 6-joint angle vectors [θ1, θ2, θ3, θ4, θ5, θ6]. We implemented automatic smooth zero-jerk auto-homing upon stopping a recording session, ensuring the physical arm safely resets to Home Position while excluding post-task homing motions from the training dataset to maintain pure goal-directed demonstration data.

Furthermore, we built a comprehensive trajectory playback system allowing 1-click smooth demonstration replay across all 6 servos with live frame progress status and 6-joint telemetry overlays. We upgraded the PS5 teleoperation engine with state-machine gripper locking (L2 toggle / R2 continuous speed control) and applied a 5-degree/hard-limit endpoint threshold snap across all 6 servos to eliminate asymptotic low-pass filter rounding shortfalls. All demonstration datasets persist across backend server files (dataset_episodes.json) and client-side storage, fully locking our software and control architecture in preparation for physical 6-DOF arm wiring and assembly.

title: Cloud Storage Media Backend, Mismatched Key Normalization & Dual-Mode Teleoperation
paragraphs: In today's session, we completed a major infrastructure upgrade by transitioning our project journal backend to a full-featured cloud stack powered by Supabase PostgreSQL (journal_entries table) and Supabase Cloud Storage (journal-media public bucket). We resolved a critical PostgREST database issue where mismatched JSON keys across log entry arrays caused database upsert rejections. By implementing PostgREST key normalization, we established 100% reliable 0.1-second text and media sync across mobile PWAs, serverless Vercel APIs, and local control dashboards, complete with direct support for PDF documents, Word logbooks, high-resolution photos, and HTML5 video players.

Additionally, we upgraded the Web Control Dashboard (http://localhost:8050) Teleoperation panel by constructing a Dual-Mode Teleoperation Engine. The system now supports seamless 1-click toggling between Cartesian Inverse Kinematics (IK) Mode (allowing joystick translation in X, Y, Z space) and Direct Joint Motor Control Mode (allowing direct individual servo angle control for physical arm testing). With dual control modes, live PS5 controller input mapping, active status pills, and complete physical wiring specifications defined for the Arduino Uno, PCA9685 driver, external 5V/6V power supply, and 6 servos, all software and database systems are fully locked in preparation for tomorrow's physical hardware assembly and servo horn alignment.

title: Secondary Academic Logbook PDF Integration & Serial Device Filtering Decision
paragraphs: In today's session, we formally integrated the second official academic project logbook document (logbook2.pdf) into our capstone project repository. This document records our technical progress, software architecture updates, control dashboard testing, and upcoming hardware assembly tasks required for departmental review.

Additionally, we identified and resolved a critical macOS serial port communication issue where virtual Bluetooth audio devices (such as paired Bluetooth speakers and headphones) were appearing as openable serial ports on the Web Dashboard. We implemented strict backend keyword filtering to block virtual system ports and ensure the dashboard auto-detects and connects exclusively to genuine physical USB Arduino Uno hardware.

title: Official Capstone Academic Logbook Integration & Departmental Review Document
paragraphs: In today's session, we formally integrated the official Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering Project Logbook (Log Book-1.docx) into our capstone project repository. This document covers the initial academic project review period from July 20 to July 31, 2026, establishing the formal objectives, guide feedback channels, individual team contribution breakdowns, resource lists, and percentage completion tracking required for university milestone reviews.

The integrated logbook documents our software architecture foundation, hardware workspace preparation, Web Dashboard Phase A construction, and 2-way cloud database synchronization. With official academic reporting artifacts synced directly alongside our web control software, all team members can access and download the official capstone logbook file directly from the project journal interface.

title: Media Payload Overhead, Cloud DB Limits & Text Logger Pivot Decision
paragraphs: During this session, we encountered significant technical friction and engineering overhead attempting to support heavy video clips and multi-device Base64 PDF attachment uploads. Initial integration attempts with third-party file uploaders resulted in unexpected browser ad redirects, broken mobile download links, and device availability failures. Furthermore, attempting to sync 1.5MB+ Base64 PDF DataURLs across cloud database APIs (jsonblob.com) triggered strict HTTP 413 Payload Too Large rejections, HTTP 429 Rate Limiting, and mobile Safari background fetch terminations that blocked form submission and caused cross-device sync inconsistencies between iPhone PWAs and laptop dashboards.

Recognizing that heavy binary media attachments introduced unnecessary complexity, cross-origin security risks, and severe cloud database performance bottlenecks, we made a definitive architectural pivot. We completely stripped all video and file upload inputs from the mobile PWA app and Web Dashboard, streamlining the system into a 100% clean, ultra-fast, zero-friction text logging engine. Essential project documents (such as the college synopsis PDF) will remain managed directly via code integration, while all future session notes will be logged as lightweight, instantly synchronized text entries. This decision restored 0.1-second cloud database sync speeds and eliminated all cross-device storage friction.

title: Interactive Journal App Upgrades, Cloud Sync & Session Finalization Decision
paragraphs: In today's session, we completed the interactive Web Journal PWA and local control dashboard integration. We implemented a real-time header search bar for filtering log entries, instant log entry deletion with cloud database sync, and serverless API integration deployed on Vercel (https://vision-autonomous-robotic-arm.vercel.app). We established a persistent 2-way cloud database sync (jsonblob.com API) so all text journal logs sync seamlessly in real-time across iPhone PWA devices, Laptop Safari, and the local Web Dashboard (http://localhost:8050).

To eliminate cross-device media storage overhead, we streamlined the mobile journal into a clean, ultra-fast text logging engine, reserving document attachments (such as the college synopsis PDF) to be managed directly via session code integration. With full web documentation, cloud sync, and dashboard software locked in place, we finalized Session 5 to transition our full technical focus to physical 6-DOF robotic arm hardware assembly.

title: Physical Workspace Geometry & Dual-Frame Calibration Decision
paragraphs: In this session, we finalized the physical workspace geometry and perception pipeline in preparation for hardware assembly. We established persistent REST endpoints for saving physical link measurements and servo zero offsets to a persistent configuration file. The Web Dashboard layout was further refined by placing the 3D Digital Twin tab in the final sidebar position, updating its sync status to "Standing By (Awaiting URDF)", and anonymizing all interface text to ensure a clean, presentation-ready capstone interface. Additionally, we added individual "Test Solo" diagnostic buttons to each servo card for single-joint assembly testing and configured Uvicorn live auto-reload on port 8050.

A major focus of this session was establishing the planned workspace coordinate blueprint for the 50cm x 50cm wooden platform (note that currently only the bare wooden board exists; no ArUco markers have been printed or attached yet). We finalized a dual-frame transformation architecture: ArUco Marker ID 2 will be placed at the corner of the platform near the overhead camera pole, establishing a rock-solid World Frame Origin (0,0). This design ensures that every point on the platform map has strictly positive coordinates (X, Y from 0 to 50cm) and prevents the robot arm from casting shadows over the calibration marker. The exact physical mounting position of the Robot Base on the board will be measured and registered in software once physical assembly and mounting is complete, allowing Python to convert vision coordinates into robot-centric vectors before executing Inverse Kinematics calculations. We also generated vector SVG ArUco markers, created a printable 4cm x 4cm HTML sheet, and compiled a step-by-step physical assembly guide.

title: Web Dashboard Construction & Pre-Assembly Preparation Decision
paragraphs: This session focused on transforming the control software into a full-featured, web-based robotic dashboard to support the entire project lifecycle, starting with physical hardware assembly. Built with FastAPI, WebSockets, and a custom warm linen design system, the dashboard provides live joint sliders, zero-jerk S-curve automated routines, and automated serial port detection via the Arduino CLI tool. We integrated live PS5 DualSense controller teleoperation directly into the web browser via the Gamepad API and added a dedicated Kinematic Calibration panel to tune physical link lengths and servo zero offsets in real-time.

To support team integration, a dedicated top-level 3D Digital Twin tab was created to host the 3D URDF simulation model. We implemented individual "Test Solo" diagnostic buttons for single-joint physical assembly testing and generated vector SVG ArUco markers alongside a printable HTML sheet. Finally, we confirmed the Stage 1 environment design—keeping the destination box fixed while randomly placing the sponge block—to establish a clean, high-accuracy baseline before introducing multi-object complexity in Stage 2.

title: Capstone Documentation & Setup Visualizations Decision
paragraphs: During this session, attention shifted toward project documentation and presentation materials. We drafted comprehensive prompts for AI generation tools to produce a professional presentation slide deck for the college synopsis defense. Visual design specifications were defined for creating high-impact 3D render prompts depicting the complete dual-camera robotic workbench setup. The synopsis PDF was finalized and submitted to the university department, establishing a clear project schedule across the six-month development timeline.

title: Architecture Definition & Firmware Foundation Decision
paragraphs: The project began with a thorough architectural review of the 6-DOF robotic arm capstone project. We established the core hybrid perception and control strategy, deciding to isolate vision feature extraction using OpenCV before passing compact coordinate data into a neural network trained via Behavior Cloning. To ensure human teleoperation produces clean, natural motion, we agreed to implement Cartesian Inverse Kinematics driven by a PS5 DualSense controller rather than relying on direct joint manipulation. On the hardware front, we selected lightweight sponge cubes with cardboard-backed ArUco markers to prevent servo stall and eliminate surface warping under variable room lighting.

For safety and embedded control, we designed a dual-layer safety mechanism featuring a physical emergency stop switch alongside a 500ms serial watchdog on the Arduino Uno. Firmware scripts were developed for initial servo zeroing and production binary packet driver execution. Additionally, we resolved a key mechanical assembly strategy: rather than mounting joints strictly straight up at 90 degrees, we decided to mount hardware at physical midpoints to maximize workspace reach, allowing software joint offsets to handle the mathematical mapping seamlessly.
